READABILITY.evidence: Names describe what they do (buildWindowsClauseSQL, validateWindowName, WindowDefinition, windowSql) and formatting matches the codebase after dprint. Each dialect hook-in is one line placed next to the matching groupBy/having code.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: The spec builder is shared in window.ts, but the ~20-line .window() body (validation, SelectionProxyHandler callback branch, push to config) is copied five times. The conventions asked for a thin method. pg/gel import buildWindowsClauseSQL via '~/sql/index.ts', so the internal helper ends up in the public barrel.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Validates window names, NaN, Infinity, negative and fractional input to preceding()/following(), from/to ordering in rows()/range(), and ntile/nthValue arguments. Numeric arguments are emitted raw, never as bound params, so params stay []. All 130 hidden fail-to-pass tests pass.

C7-01-CASE1.evidence: Purely additive: `export * from './window.ts'`, an optional `windows?: WindowDefinition[]` on all five *SelectConfig types, and the same .window() on pg/mysql/sqlite/singlestore/gel. windowSql is undefined when unused, so generated SQL for existing queries is unchanged. All 566 existing (pass-to-pass) tests still pass.
